scope: Theorem 8.1 (Constant-arc arch estimate) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants M > 1, c, C > 0, and a positive geometric tolerance with the following property. Fix a positive integer N and scales 16r < ℓ1 < · · · < ℓN < R/10, ℓi+1 ≥ Mℓi. (8.2) Suppose that, in QR, the limiting boundary is the single graph y = f(x), with f(0) = f′(0) = 0 and ∥f′∥∞ smaller than the geometric tolerance, and that its inward side is above this graph. The original polygon boundary is a sufficiently fine uniform parametric approximation of this arc and has the same inside and outside away from its shrinking boundary neighborhood. Its approximation error, divided by ℓ1, tends to zero. A smooth boundary has these properties after decreasing the fixed outer scale. Allow, in addition, a fixed finite number of boundary-attached patch replacements as above, whose diameters are sufficiently small relative to the selected scales. Suppose that the actual usable boundary data satisfy η ≥ k − 2 everywhere, η ≥ k on the usable boundary in QR \ Qr, (8.3) where k ∈ Z. For sufficiently small mesh and sufficiently fine boundary and replacement approxi- mations, Pη ( an arch at threshold k surrounds Qr in QR ) ≥ 1 − Ce−cN . (8.4) The constants do not depend on the boundary heights or on the number of vertices in a boundary or separator. They also do not depend on the fixed number of tiny replacements; the required approximation accuracy may do so. There is a reversed statement with η ≤ k + 2, clean data η ≤ k, and a separator at height at most k.
